fact_text: Special situations such as acquisitions and delistings often give minority shareholders a value-realisation event, which the analyst treats as a recurring source of short-term gains on the PSX.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX delisting rules require the offer to minority shareholders to be at least the highest share price of the last three years, and the per-share value from an independent intrinsic valuation is a further requirement.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A delisting requires the buyer to acquire almost all minority shares, so the minimum-price rules effectively set what every remaining minority holder receives.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A delisting process typically completes in about three to six months, so a delisting offer well above the market price is a short-duration trade rather than a long hold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In an acquisition the new buyer must acquire at least 50% of shares, and the price to minority holders must meet thresholds based on the buyer's offer price, recent average prices, and book value for thinly traded stocks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Acquisitions take about a year on average because competition and other regulators must approve them, and some deals fall through, so the payoff is slower than in a delisting.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For a takeover candidate, estimate intrinsic value from the replacement cost of plant and land, earnings power at roughly 10 to 15 times profit for asset-light firms, and the number of interested bidders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Old land recorded at historical cost in a company's books is often a hidden asset that the share price does not reflect, and an independent valuation usually includes it at market value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Pak Suzuki Motor's delisting, the approved buyback price was far below the analyst's intrinsic estimate despite prime land held at old cost, so investors who relied on rumoured higher prices lost money.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a partial acquisition the market price can settle well below the deal price even when the offer is double the market price, because the buyer only takes about half the shares at the offer price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On any delisting or acquisition announcement, first compute the one, three and six month average share prices and the highest price of the last three years, then check the balance sheet for hidden asset value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects roughly two to three special-situation opportunities a year on the PSX from delistings and acquisitions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 2007 study cited by the analyst put Warren Buffett's annual return near 39%, falling to about 26% when his special-situation investments are excluded.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Special Situations in Pakistan' (YouTube transcript, undated)
